newsitem.title: HONG KONG: PRESS DIGEST - HK newspaper headlines - Dec 10.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - HK newspaper headlines - Dec 10.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Hong Kong press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

-- EXPRESS NEWS -- A trade report showed that Hong Kong would have a shortfall of 20,000 labourers in the next year. If the problem was not solved, Hong Kong's overall construction plan would be postponed, the paper said.
-- MING PAO DAILY -- One hundred and thirty four people applied to compete for the 60 seats on the provisional legislature. Of the 134, 29 were members of the Preparatory Committee.
-- The estimated number of newspapers and magazines in China next year would be more than 10,000. Last year alone, 39 new publications were set up.
-- HONG KONG ECONOMIC TIMES -- The government is studying and making long-term plans to stabilise local property prices, including increasing land supply and accelerating the approval process.
-- HONG KONG ECONOMIC JOURNAL -- Property analysts believed that property speculation might spread into small and medium-sized flat market.
-- TA KUNG PAO -- The Chinese air force had mastered new fighting skills and had certain long-distance fighting ability.

-- SOUTH CHINA MORNING POST -- China's November industrial output -- up 13.4 percent year-on-year -- continued the strong rebound of the summer amid signs Beijing will push for greater economic growth next year.

-- The representative bodies of Asia's main airlines launched a stinging attack on Hong Kong's Airport Authority, hinting it was trying to stall the disclosure of fee levels at the new Chek Lap Kok airport.
-- HONGKONG STANDARD -- Tycoon Jimmy Lai planned to tap the stock market for funds by floating his wholly owned FT Holdings, an artificial Christmas tree maker.
